summary: Frontend-only verification of the trailing-slash auth-redirect bug fix. Confirmed that ALL auth redirects (session-expired auth gate, post-login, profile navigation, header logout) now navigate to URLs WITH trailing slashes and never leak the :8080 internal port. The load-bearing necessary condition for defeating the production 301 chain that stranded users at http://lab.bashari.co:8080/login/ is satisfied.
critical_code_review_comments: dashboard/layout.tsx uses two different logout paths: the sidebar Logout button calls handleLogout() (which does logout() + window.location.replace('/login/')), while the header profile-menu Logout inlines `logout(); window.location.replace('/login/');`. Both are functionally equivalent post-fix, but they are separate copies of the same 3-line snippet — consolidate to a single handler to keep the trailing-slash invariant in one place (Test 3/4 confirmed both currently work).

The header profile-menu 'My Profile' still uses router.push('/dashboard/profile/') (slashed) while every other auth-critical redirect switched to window.location.replace. The router.push works here because it stays on the client-side SPA route (no ingress round-trip), so no port-leak risk — but the pattern inconsistency invites future regressions. Consider a shared helper `navigateToSlashed(path)` and document the invariant.

next.config.mjs's `trailingSlash: true` is now load-bearing but only enforced by convention in code. A pre-commit grep/lint rule ('no router.push/replace or window.location.replace target ending without /') would prevent this class of bug from re-appearing.
test_credentials: admin@bashari.com / admin123 (super_admin). Login went through /api/auth/login (backend TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY is blank so no captcha token needed). Automated browser login used in-browser fetch to /api/auth/login + sessionStorage injection of BOTH 'token' key AND the zustand 'auth-storage' blob (required — the axios request interceptor reads sessionStorage['token'] while the DashboardLayout auth gate reads the zustand blob).
seed_data_creation: None. All tests used existing admin account and read-only navigation.
context_for_next_testing_agent: For any future auth-flow testing on this app, inject BOTH sessionStorage['token'] and sessionStorage['auth-storage'] — missing the raw 'token' key causes background API calls (branches/pending access requests) to fire un-authorized, tripping the axios 401 interceptor and bouncing the tab to /login/?reason=expired within seconds. The trailing-slash discipline (next.config.mjs sets trailingSlash: true) is now load-bearing for production — every router.push/replace or window.location.replace target must end with '/'. STATIC-BUILD grep search confirms no slashless redirect targets remain in /app/frontend/src (only surviving occurrences of '/login' without trailing slash in built JS are (a) pathname.startsWith('/login') in api.ts — a check, not a redirect, and (b) the substring inside '/login/?reason=expired' and a display string 'children:"/login"' — both fine).

test_results_detail.head_requests_to_slashed_paths: {'/login/': 200, '/dashboard/': 200, '/dashboard/profile/': 200} — all three routes are served as static index.html files from build/, so the browser never hits the ingress 301 chain in the first place on preview.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: next.config.mjs sets trailingSlash: true (so `next build` writes each route as `<route>/index.html`) and the production nginx does CRA-style `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html` — matching a directory with an index.html, not a `.html` extension. When a slashless path (e.g. `/login`) hits production ingress, ingress issues a 301 to the absolute URL of the directory (`http://lab.bashari.co:8080/login/`), leaking the internal listen port + downgrading protocol from https to http, which the browser refuses. In `dashboard/layout.tsx`, `router.replace('/login')` (no slash) was called from three sites (auth-gate useEffect, handleLogout, header profile-menu Logout). When the tab sat idle overnight and the sessionStorage 'auth-storage' blob's `isAuthenticated` reset (or was cleared by the axios 401 interceptor after a background poll like refreshPendingAccess), the auth-gate useEffect fired the slashless redirect and stranded the user. Mitigation (verified): all three sites now use `window.location.replace('/login/')` (with trailing slash) — same pattern as `lib/api.ts` line 98 which was already correct. Analogous secondary fixes applied to login/page.tsx (post-login → '/dashboard/' / '/dashboard/signing-pad/') and setup-password/page.tsx (→ '/dashboard/'). Static-build grep confirms zero slashless redirect targets remain.
